sentences.text: Acidaminococcus is a genus of strictly anaerobic, Gram-negative cocci that forms part of the normal flora of the gastrointestinal tract.
A strain isolated from the feces of an adult in the Republic of Korea, matching the genus Acidaminococcus, used glutamic acid as its primary energy source and produced acetic and butyric acid.
A study of 26 patients with solid tumours reported that the proportion of Acidaminococcus was significantly higher in patients who developed immune-related adverse events than in those who did not.
A cross-sectional analysis of 114 women reported that visceral adipose tissue was correlated with the abundance of the Acidaminococcus genus.
